pharm: Antipseudomonal ureidopenicillin; bactericidal beta-lactam that inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis with broad Gram-negative coverage including Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
quick: 3-4 g IV/IM q4-6h (12-18 g/day); max ~24 g/day
Category B; considered acceptable when indicated
Excreted in low concentrations; use with caution
No specific scheme; monitor LFTs on prolonged therapy
Coagulation, electrolytes (sodium/potassium), renal and hepatic function
summary: Piperacillin is an extended-spectrum antipseudomonal ureidopenicillin given IV or IM for serious infections, including those caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Note this is plain piperacillin, not the piperacillin-tazobactam combination, so it lacks beta-lactamase inhibitor coverage and is dosed in piperacillin units (3-4 g). It requires renal dose adjustment, carries a risk of hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis, delivers a substantial sodium load, and can cause bleeding/platelet dysfunction at high doses. It must not be mixed in the same line as aminoglycosides.
indications: Complicated and uncomplicated urinary tract infections
Infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa and other susceptible Gram-negative bacilli

dosage.n: Most common regimen; max usual ~24 g/day

dosage.t: Once, with probenecid 1 g PO ~30 min before

dosage.d: CrCl 20-40: 12 g/day (4 g q8h); CrCl <20: 8 g/day (4 g q12h)
dosage.n: Hemodialysis: max 6 g/day plus 1 g after each dialysis

admin: IV: give as a slow push over 3-5 minutes or by infusion over 20-30 minutes
IM: reconstitute and inject no more than 2 g per site into the upper-outer gluteal quadrant
Do not mix piperacillin and aminoglycosides in the same syringe or infusion line (mutual inactivation)
Usual course is 7-10 days; continue at least 48-72 hours after the patient is asymptomatic; at least 10 days for streptococcal infections
Discard reconstituted solution after 24 hours at room temperature or 48 hours refrigerated
moa: Piperacillin is bactericidal; it binds penicillin-binding proteins (transpeptidases) and inhibits the final cross-linking step of bacterial cell-wall peptidoglycan synthesis, leading to cell lysis. Its acylureido side chain confers extended activity against Gram-negative organisms including Pseudomonas.

absolute: History of allergic reaction to any beta-lactam (penicillins or cephalosporins)
relative: Renal impairment (bleeding risk and dose reduction)

preg: Pregnancy Category B - no evidence of harm in animal studies; no adequate controlled human studies. Use when clearly indicated.
lact: Excreted in low concentrations in human milk; use with caution (monitor the infant for diarrhea, candidiasis, or rash).
renal: Requires dose reduction or extended dosing interval based on creatinine clearance; piperacillin is predominantly excreted unchanged in urine. Hemodialysis removes the drug (give a supplemental dose after dialysis); peritoneal dialysis does not.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment scheme; reversible elevations in transaminases and bilirubin and rare cholestatic hepatitis can occur, so monitor liver function on prolonged therapy.

major: Aminoglycosides - mutual inactivation if mixed in the same line (give separately)
Methotrexate - reduced excretion and increased toxicity
moderate: Probenecid - increases and prolongs piperacillin levels (sometimes used intentionally)
Vecuronium and other neuromuscular blockers - prolonged blockade
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine glucose (copper-reduction methods), positive direct Coombs test, and false-positive Aspergillus galactomannan assays.

serious: Bleeding and abnormal platelet aggregation (high dose, renal failure)

monitoring: Coagulation parameters (PT, bleeding/clotting time, platelet function) - especially in renal impairment
Serum electrolytes including sodium and potassium
Hepatic and hematopoietic function on prolonged therapy
Syphilis serology at 3 months when treating gonorrhea
counsel: Tell your clinician about any penicillin or cephalosporin allergy before treatment
Report rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing immediately
Report persistent or bloody diarrhea, which can occur even weeks after treatment
Complete the full prescribed course even if you feel better
pk: End of IV infusion; IM ~30-50 min
~1 hour (54-63 min); prolonged in renal impairment
20-25 C; reconstituted solution per label (24 h RT / 48 h refrigerated)
pearls: This is plain piperacillin, not piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn) - verify the product and that doses are in piperacillin units
Its defining role is antipseudomonal coverage among the penicillins
Synergistic with aminoglycosides against Pseudomonas, but never mix them in the same line
Delivers ~1.85 mEq of sodium per gram - a meaningful sodium load at high doses
High doses in renal failure can cause bleeding (platelet dysfunction) and seizures (neurotoxicity)
missed: Hospital-administered parenteral antibiotic; if a dose is delayed, give it as soon as recognized and resume the schedule. Do not double the dose. Notify the treating team if the timing is significantly altered.
overdose: No specific antidote. High concentrations, especially in renal impairment, may cause neuromuscular hyperirritability and seizures. Discontinue the drug and provide supportive care; piperacillin is removed by hemodialysis (not peritoneal dialysis).
